thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 Severity: page — Canary rollout 2026-03-15-v2 causing tail latency spike (p99) and streaming stalls in us-east-1. Auto-alert: p99 > 1500ms.

maria: I'm oncall. Seeing p95 up from 120ms -> 900ms, p99 ~ 1.8s and streaming stall count spiking. Metrics dashboard: https://console.redwood/infracloud/edges/rollouts/2026-03-15-v2

josh: Confirmed. Top signal: streaming token lag on multiplex workers, KV cache miss rate up 4x, some CPU steal on encoder nodes.

kyla: Any recent infra changes? Autoscaler logs look normal. Was a traffic shift to canary at 10% about 12m ago.

maria: Yep, we ramped canary to 10% at 16:02 UTC. Before that p99 stable ~110ms.

ops_lead: Paging for triage. @maria take lead, @josh investigate KV/cache, @kyla check rollout config and traffic shaping, I'll coordinate rollback if needed. Sam from CS on standby for customer impact.

sam-cs: Customer note: Corgata reported streaming responses hanging ~25–30s around 16:08 UTC, they just filed a ticket.

josh: I pulled a tail-sample from streaming workers: frequent stalls waiting on remote KV reads. Pattern: spike in KV latency (95th ~120ms -> 1.2s) and transient queueing inside encoder pool.

maria: Quick mitigation options: 1) throttle canary back to 1–2% 2) failover canary traffic to stable model 3) rollback canary release. Prefer least-impact first.

kyla: Traffic policy shows live fallback enabled but not hit because the model versions are deemed compatible; fallback threshold set high (p99 > 3s). We can lower threshold to trigger fallback faster.

deploy-bot: exec: `redwoodctl rollout update --id canary-20260315-v2 --traffic 2%` queued.

maria: Doing traffic -> 2% now.

(30s later)

josh: After throttle: p95 dropped to ~220ms, p99 ~650ms, streaming stall count decreased ~70%. KV miss rate still elevated but less bursty.

ops_lead: Good containment but still borderline. We need root cause: is this model bigger memory/KV footprint causing eviction thrash? Anyone have model shapes?

josh: Comparing checkpoints: v2 has wider attention window and slightly larger KV per token; combined with small worker batch size increased memory pressure. Metrics show >30% increase in KV evictions per host.

maria: Given customer impact and persistent KV thrash, recommend rollback to stable and open a postmortem. We should also schedule a lightweight canary with offline shadowing before re-roll.

deploy-bot: exec: `redwoodctl rollout rollback --id canary-20260315-v2 --target stable-20260314` started.

(1m)

kyla: Rollback in progress, traffic shift 2% -> 0% then to stable. Watching draining connections.

sam-cs: Corgata confirms latency back to normal after ~2m from rollback start. They saw degraded UX but no data loss. Sam to follow up with incident email.

maria: Oncall handoff notes for next: - Rollout triggered at 16:02 UTC -> p99 spike by 16:07 - Throttle to 2% at 16:09 reduced impact - Rollback initiated 16:12, stable restored by 16:15 - Affected region: us-east-1 - Customers flagged: Corgata (severe), internal canary tests (several).

ops_lead: Next action items: 1) postmortem owner @josh 2) create ticket to add KV eviction guardrail in runtime (auto-reject if estimated KV growth > X%) 3) add shadow-only ramp for larger models 4) tighter live-fallback thresholds for streaming paths.

josh: Will own postmortem. I'll attach kernel and eviction traces, batch-size perf tests, and suggest quantization/worker config changes.

maria: Thanks all. If anything else pops, re-open thread. :thumbsup:
